bibl.title: Brain activity during intra- and cross-modal priming: new empirical data and review of the literature

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: A straightforward result of the present study is that auditory-to-auditory within-modality and auditory-to-visual cross-modality stem completion priming are associated with distinct patterns of rCBF changes as detected by PET.

span.label: repetition priming
span.quote: Repetition priming is a form of implicit memory that typically manifests as a facilitation in re-processing recently experienced stimuli or as a bias in completing fragments with recently encountered items when test instructions do not make any reference to prior events.

span.label: pet-imaging
span.quote: A positron emission tomography (PET) study was conducted to investigate the neurofunctional correlate of auditory within-modality and auditory-to-visual cross-modality stem completion priming.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The left inferior temporal/fusiform region mediates interaction between phonological and orthographic word codes, and this shared abstract code is what carries facilitation across modalities
span.quote: In particular, it suggests that this cortical region might be involved in the complex interactions between the phonological and orthographic codes of words which ultimately allow for the cross-modality facilitation in verbal stimulus re-processing.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Right prefrontal increases arise from post-retrieval awareness that the generated word was recently encountered (involuntary conscious memory), not from deliberate episodic search driving the completions
span.quote: The substantially low level of the completion rate and the lack of an increase in priming magnitude across successive study-test blocks suggest that the contribution of such mechanisms is more in eliciting post-retrieval awareness of a recent encounter with the generated word than in actual support for active retrieval.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Left prefrontal increases reflect more efficient access to output lexical representations of recently encountered words rather than generic word-fluency demand
span.quote: Rather, rCBF changes in this region should be considered as the expression of more efficient access to output representations of recently encountered words prompted by either phonological or semantic cues.

span.label: The cross-modality parietal and temporal activations cannot be attributed a specific role because the interaction contrasts were not significant.
span.quote: Also in this case, however, the lack of significance of the interaction contrasts suggests caution in attributing a peculiar role of this cluster of activations in the genesis of cross-modality priming.

span.label: The left prefrontal activation specific to within-modality priming is only suggestive, again because the interaction failed.
span.quote: For this reason, the peculiarity of left prefrontal activation in the within-modality priming can be regarded as only suggestive.

span.label: The comparability of the two priming effects may be an artefact of a chance difference in the auditory baseline completion rate.
span.quote: However, it should be noted that the stem completion rate with target words during auditory baseline scans (3.9) was (likely by chance) quite a bit higher than during visual baseline scans (3.2; P = 0.10).

span.label: the 30-word stimulus sets were counterbalanced across subjects so each occurred equally often in the within- and cross-modality conditions and in the priming and baseline scans
span.note: eliminates: that a condition difference is a difference between the word sets
span.quote: The stimuli were counterbalanced across subjects so that each 30-word set occurred equally often in the within and cross-modality condition, priming and baseline scans.

span.label: condition and scan order counterbalanced across blocks and subjects in a LATIN SQUARE design
span.note: eliminates: that the effect is an order effect across the scanning session
span.quote: The order of within and cross-modality conditions as well as priming and baseline scans was also counterbalanced across blocks and subjects (Latin square design).

span.label: a postscan debriefing asked whether subjects had noticed that some stems came from the study list - and NEARLY ALL OF THEM HAD
span.note: eliminates: that the priming is implicit - the control was run to establish that subjects were unaware, and it established the opposite
span.quote: Moreover, informal assessment of subjects during postscan debriefing revealed that nearly all subjects in both withinand cross-modality conditions were aware of the fact that some of the stems came from the study list.

span.label: repetition priming
span.quote: Repetition priming is a form of implicit memory that typically manifests as a facilitation in re-processing recently experienced stimuli or as a bias in completing fragments with recently encountered items when test instructions do not make any reference to prior events.

span.label: implicit memory
span.quote: Repetition priming is a form of implicit memory that typically manifests as a facilitation in re-processing recently experienced stimuli or as a bias in completing fragments with recently encountered items when test instructions do not make any reference to prior events.

span.label: within-modality
span.quote: Instead, within-modality auditory priming was associated with a bilateral pattern of prefrontal rCBF increase.

span.label: modality
span.quote: In most cases, the magnitude of the priming effect is larger when the same modality of stimulus presentation is used for study and testing than when it differs (Graf, Mandler, & Haden, 1982).

span.label: **THE ASYMMETRY IS STATED AS SETTLED BACKGROUND, AND THREE YEARS LATER IT IS AN ARTEFACT.** `In most cases, the magnitude of the priming effect is LARGER when the same modality of stimulus presentation is used for study and testing than when it differs (Graf, Mandler, & Haden, 1982).` Written as review, not as a claim under test - which is what makes it worth tagging. **lukatela2007 minimised study-test asymmetries across five experiments and found EQUAL magnitudes**, with the conventional advantage returning only in a within-subjects design. Kirsner1986 reasons from the asymmetry; this record goes looking for its brain basis; lukatela2007 dissolves it. **Three records, one day, none citing the others**
span.quote: In most cases, the magnitude of the priming effect is larger when the same modality of stimulus presentation is used for study and testing than when it differs (Graf, Mandler, & Haden, 1982).

span.label: **AND THE NEURAL RESULT IS A DISSOCIATION IN DIRECTION, NOT JUST IN LOCATION:** cross-modal priming gave a larger rCBF DECREASE in left inferior temporal and fusiform cortex - regions tied to modality-independent lexical retrieval - while `WITHIN-MODALITY auditory priming was associated with a bilateral pattern of prefrontal rCBF INCREASE.` Different regions and opposite signs. **Whatever the behavioural asymmetry turns out to be, these two conditions are not one process running at two strengths in this data** - which is a constraint that survives even if lukatela2007 is right that the behavioural difference is a design artefact
span.quote: Instead, within-modality auditory priming was associated with a bilateral pattern of prefrontal rCBF increase.

span.label: **THE DEFINITION PUTS THE CRITERION IN THE INSTRUCTIONS, WHICH IS EASY TO READ PAST:** repetition priming manifests as facilitation or a completion bias `WHEN TEST INSTRUCTIONS DO NOT MAKE ANY REFERENCE TO PRIOR EVENTS.` Not `when the subject is unaware`, not `when memory is not consciously used` - **when the experimenter did not mention it.** The construct is operationalised by what was said to the participant, and the 90%% discussion of this same paper concedes that `involuntary conscious memory` may occur anyway when the study context is reinstated. The definition and the caveat are in the same paper
span.quote: Repetition priming is a form of implicit memory that typically manifests as a facilitation in re-processing recently experienced stimuli or as a bias in completing fragments with recently encountered items when test instructions do not make any reference to prior events.

span.label: contradicts → Badgaiyan et al. (1999); Badgaiyan et al. (2001)
span.quote: This is in contrast with previous reports in the literature which showed rCBF decreases in the lateral occipital cortex (BA 19) during auditory stem completion priming (Badgaiyan et al., 1999; Badgaiyan et al., 2001).

span.label: contradicts → Carlesimo, Marfia, Loasses, & Caltagirone (1996); Graf et al. (1985)
span.quote: Previous behavioural studies consistently reported significantly larger within-modality than cross-modality stem completion priming (e.g. Carlesimo, Marfia, Loasses, & Caltagirone, 1996; Graf et al., 1985).

span.label: contradicts → Badgaiyan et al. (1999); Schacter et al. (1999)
span.quote: However, the conclusion that cross-modality priming is more exposed to contamination by explicit retrieval strategies than within-modality priming is not supported by neuropsychological evidence.

span.label: builds-on → Buckner et al. (2000)
span.quote: Support for the view that regions in the left inferior temporal cortex can modulate their neural activity in response to verbal stimuli independent of stimulus-driven perceptual processes comes from an fMRI study by Buckner et al. (2000).

span.label: repetition priming —is-a→ implicit memory
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95 — **THE CLEANEST `is-a` I HAVE CUT THIS SESSION, AND THEY ARE RARE.** `Repetition priming IS A FORM OF implicit memory` - the relation is the sentence's main verb, both endpoints are named as words, and there is no hedge to preserve. Weight 0.95. Most taxonomy in this literature has to be inferred from how terms are used together; here it is asserted directly, in an introduction, as the thing the reader is expected to already accept.
span.quote: Repetition priming is a form of implicit memory that typically manifests as a facilitation in re-processing recently experienced stimuli or as a bias in completing fragments with recently encountered items when test instructions do not make any reference to prior events.

span.label: within-modality —operationalised-as→ modality
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.85 — **WEAK ON PURPOSE, AND THE WEAKNESS IS WHERE THE SPAN STOPS.** The quote names the condition and its neural correlate; it does not define what `within-modality` means. That definition is in the methods, in a sentence carrying stereotactic coordinates that the table guard refuses. Weight 0.85 and the confidence at 0.95 only because the endpoint attestation is exact - `within-modality` is a word of this span and `modality` is inside it as a word too. **A reader taking this triple alone learns that the two are related and not how**, which the note has to say out loud.
span.quote: Instead, within-modality auditory priming was associated with a bilateral pattern of prefrontal rCBF increase.

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: These data were analysed by means of a three-way ANOVA with modality of stem presentation (auditory versus visual), condition (priming versus baseline) and block (from 1 to 3) as repeated factors.

span.label: F-test
span.quote: The modality effect was significant (F = 16.8; P < 0.01 with d.f. = 1, 7).

span.label: t-test
span.quote: Global differences in CBF across conditions were made using the t statistic (Friston et al., 1995a).

span.label: z-score
span.quote: The resulting set of t values constituted a statistical parametric map (SPM{t}) which was transformed into Z score maps (SPM{Z}).

span.label: general linear model
span.quote: Statistical analyses were performed according to the SPM96 implementation of the general linear model (Fletcher, Shallice, Frith, Frackowiak, & Dolan, 1996).

span.label: random effects analysis
span.quote: We also performed a random effect analysis of PET data and found

span.label: p-value
span.quote: We first calculated the simple effects of the rCBF changes (both increases and decreases) associated with the priming effects (priming minus baseline scans) (statistical threshold one-tailed, P < 0.001 uncorrected).

span.label: correlation
span.quote: The rate of rCBF decrease in this area showed a significant negative correlation with the amount of cross-modality priming, as measured behaviourally (x = −50; y = −48; z = −20; Z = 2.0; P = 0.02) (Fig. 1).

span.label: meta-analysis
span.quote: To ease a comparison of the present results with the results previously reported in the literature, a meta-analysis of the activation and de-activation patterns is shown in Table 3.

span.label: Auditory-to-visual cross-modality priming produced a significantly larger blood-flow decrease at the left inferior temporal/fusiform boundary than within-modality auditory priming.
span.quote: Compared to the auditory-to-auditory priming condition, cross-modality priming was associated with a significantly larger regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF) decrease at the boundary between left inferior temporal and fusiform gyri, brain regions previously associated with modality independent lexical retrieval and reading.

span.label: The interaction analysis confirmed the deactivation difference was specific to the cross-modality condition in left BA 37/20.
span.quote: Conversely, there was an area of significantly larger rCBF decrease in the cross-modality condition at the junction between the left fusiform and inferior temporal gyrus (BA 37/20).

span.label: Within-modality auditory priming was accompanied by bilateral prefrontal blood-flow increases rather than posterior deactivations.
span.quote: Comparison of priming and baseline scans in the withinmodality auditory condition show a pattern of bilateral prefrontal rCBF increases in the left inferior frontal gyrus (BA 46) and in the right superior (BA 9) and middle (BA 10) frontal gyri.

span.label: Right middle frontal activation was significantly greater for within-modality than for cross-modality priming, the reverse of what earlier studies had reported.
span.quote: The analysis showed a significantly greater activation in the right middle frontal gyrus (BA 9) in the within-modality than in the cross-modality condition.

span.label: Behaviourally the within- and cross-modality priming effects did not differ in size, contrary to the usual finding of a within-modality advantage.
span.quote: The condition and modality effects did not interact significantly (F = 0.4; P = n.s. with d.f. = 1, 7), thus revealing comparably sized priming effects in the withinand cross-modality conditions (4.4 and 3.9).

span.label: The magnitude of the left inferior temporal deactivation tracked each subject's behavioural cross-modality priming, tying the imaging effect to behaviour.
span.quote: The rate of rCBF decrease in this area showed a significant negative correlation with the amount of cross-modality priming, as measured behaviourally (x = −50; y = −48; z = −20; Z = 2.0; P = 0.02) (Fig. 1).

span.label: No blood-flow decreases reached the conventional threshold for within-modality auditory priming, unlike previous auditory stem-completion PET reports.
span.quote: There were no significant rCBF decreases related to within-modality priming using this threshold.

span.label: Priming magnitude did not grow across successive study-test blocks, arguing against subjects adopting explicit retrieval strategies.
span.quote: The Block effect was not significant (F = 0.7; P = n.s. with d.f. = 2, 14) and did not interact reliably with any of the other factors, thus demonstrating that the size of the priming effect was similar across replications.

span.label: repetition priming
span.quote: Repetition priming is a form of implicit memory that typically manifests as a facilitation in re-processing recently experienced stimuli or as a bias in completing fragments with recently encountered items when test instructions do not make any reference to prior events.

span.label: cross-modality priming
span.quote: However, significant cross-modality priming (i.e. facilitated re-processing of items previously experienced in a different modality) is also commonly observed

span.label: stem completion paradigm
span.quote: In a typical stem completion paradigm, subjects are first exposed to a list of words.

span.label: within-modality priming effect (operational definition)
span.quote: The within-modality priming effect was measured as the difference between the number of auditorily presented stems that were completed with a target word from a studied list and the number of stems that were casually completed with a target word from an unstudied list.

span.label: basal temporal language area
span.quote: the term “basal temporal language area” was proposed to define a cortical region involving the left fusiform, inferior temporal and parahippocampal gyri.

span.label: involuntary conscious memory
span.quote: Schacter (1987) coined the expression “involuntary conscious memory” to describe this phenomenon.

span.label: modality of stem presentation (auditory versus visual)
span.term: modality of stem presentation (auditory versus visual)
span.quote: These data were analysed by means of a three-way ANOVA with modality of stem presentation (auditory versus visual), condition (priming versus baseline) and block (from 1 to 3) as repeated factors.

span.label: study status of the stems (studied versus unstudied words)
span.term: study status of the stems (studied versus unstudied words)
span.quote: The analysis was based on a 2 (auditory versus visual modality of stem presentation) × 2 (studied versus unstudied words) factorial design.

span.label: regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF)
span.quote: The integrated counts accumulated over 90 s scans were used as an index of rCBF.

span.label: proportion of stems completed with target words
span.term: proportion of stems completed with target words
span.quote: The percentage of target words used to complete word stems in the priming and baseline scans of the withinand cross-modality conditions are reported in Table 1.

span.label: foil lists matched to targets for length and frequency
span.term: foil lists matched to targets for length and frequency
span.quote: Constraints regarding the selection of words for the foil lists were that they should be comparable in length and frequency to and not share their initial three letters with the experimental target words.

span.label: counterbalancing of condition and scan order across subjects
span.term: counterbalancing of condition and scan order across subjects
span.quote: The order of within and cross-modality conditions as well as priming and baseline scans was also counterbalanced across blocks and subjects (Latin square design).

span.label: Eight — number of participants scanned (male college students aged 20-27)
span.quote: Eight male college students (age range: 20–27) participated in the study.

span.label: 12 scans — number of PET scans per subject, three in each of the four conditions
span.quote: Each subject underwent 12 scans, three in each of the four conditions

span.label: 360 — number of common Italian target words making up the stem-completion materials
span.quote: Target materials for the stem completion test consisted of a list of 360 common Italian words, 4–11 letters in length.

span.label: 6.51 per million — mean lexical frequency of the target words in Italian
span.quote: Frequency of occurrence of these words in the Italian language ranged from 0 to 23 with a mean of 6.51 per million

span.label: 7.7 versus 3.5 — mean number of stems completed with target words in priming versus baseline scans
span.quote: More stems were completed with target words during the priming than the baseline scans (7.7 versus 3.5).

span.label: 4.4 and 3.9 — size of the within-modality and cross-modality priming effects, which did not differ reliably
span.quote: The condition and modality effects did not interact significantly (F = 0.4; P = n.s. with d.f. = 1, 7), thus revealing comparably sized priming effects in the withinand cross-modality conditions (4.4 and 3.9).

span.label: F = 42.2; P < 0.001 — main effect of condition (priming versus baseline) on stem completion
span.quote: The condition effect was also significant (F = 42.2; P < 0.001 with d.f. = 1, 7).

span.label: Z = 2.59 — sub-threshold deactivation peak in right BA 19 for within-modality auditory priming, found only in an exploratory analysis
span.quote: an area of rCBF suppression in priming with respect to the baseline condition emerged in right BA 19 (x = 48; y = −84; z = 12; Z = 2.59)

span.label: Z = 2.0; P = 0.02 — strength of the correlation between left BA 37/20 deactivation and behavioural cross-modality priming
span.quote: The rate of rCBF decrease in this area showed a significant negative correlation with the amount of cross-modality priming, as measured behaviourally (x = −50; y = −48; z = −20; Z = 2.0; P = 0.02) (Fig. 1).
